podcast.title: Replaced Tom DeLonge in Blink 182 (2015)
podcast.body: In March 2015, Matt Skiba was brought in from Alkaline Trio to replace Tom DeLonge in Blink 182. After performing three initial gigs, starting March 18, 2015, he was made an official member of the band. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Not Sober During "Nine" Production (2019)
podcast.body: During the period surrounding the creation of Blink 182's *Nine* album, Matt Skiba was not sober, paralleling a similar struggle experienced by Mark Hoppus at the time. "Same thing with Mads Keeba."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Last Show with Blink 182 (2020)
podcast.body: Matt Skiba's final performance with Blink 182 occurred on January 18, 2020, in Los Angeles, just before the global COVID-19 pandemic caused widespread shutdowns. His absence from the song "Quarantine," released later that year, was noted. "And that also turned out to be the last show with Mads Keeba."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Graceful Departure from Blink 182 (2022)
podcast.body: Upon the announcement of Tom DeLonge's return to Blink 182, Matt Skiba handled the situation "like a pro." He was aware the announcement was forthcoming, accepted the circumstances gracefully, and extended his congratulations and thanks to the band members for the opportunity he had been given. "Matskiba took it like a pro. He knew the announcement was coming. He accepted the situation gracefully and congratulated the guys and thanked them for the opportunity of being in the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Filling In for Tom DeLonge
podcast.body: In March 2015, Max Schieber (guitarist for Alkaline Trio) stepped in to play with Blink-182 for two club shows following Tom DeLonge's second departure. Lawyers subsequently worked to formalize Tom's exit and Max's position within the band. "Max Schieber, the guitarist for a band called Alkaline Trio filled in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Matt Skiba's Recruitment and First Performance (2015)
xref.body: After Tom DeLonge's second departure, Mark Hoppus and Travis Barker decided against disbanding Blink 182 and recruited Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio. Their first performance with Skiba on March 18, 2015, marked the first time Mark Hoppus played in Blink without Tom DeLonge, after which Skiba was made an official member. "Mark and Travis had no plans to kill Blink so they brought in Matt Skiba from Alkaline Trio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Max Schieber Joins (2015)
xref.body: In March 2015, following Tom Delonge's second departure, Blink-182 played two club shows with Max Schieber (likely Matt Skiba) of Alkaline Trio filling in as guitarist. Lawyers worked to formalize Tom's exit and Max's integration into the band. "In March 2015, Blink played two club shows without Tom. Max Schieber, the guitarist for a band called Alkaline Trio filled in."

xref.body: The band's last live performance before the COVID-19 pandemic, held in Los Angeles on January 18, 2020, also turned out to be the final show featuring Matt Skiba as a member of Blink 182. "Blinks last show before everything hit the fan was in Los Angeles on January 18, 2020. And that also turned out to be the last show with Mads Keeba."
